propositions: GitHub Actions pytest matrix jobs became stuck at 99% progress for 1.7–4.3 hours when patchsets omitted blob-prefetch fix 96a0d5c3f, causing per-blob lazy-fetch RPCs to timeout; manual cancellation was required to clear the queue.

The reusable workflow jobs.test in _build-and-test.yml lacked a timeout-minutes bound, allowing GitHub's 360-minute default to permit hours-long hangs; adding timeout-minutes: 60 ensures job termination within a healthy bound while preserving >3x margin over documented 10–16m execution.

Gerrit 1129 test_comment_map_matches_the_shared_contract hung because FakeJiraClient.search_issues ignored startAt/maxResults pagination kwargs and returned the same non-empty issue list forever, creating an infinite loop in the paged-search caller; slicing the fake result by pagination offset resolved the hang.

Affected patchsets 1129/1130/1131/1136 omitted merged commit 96a0d5c3f (747f blob-prefetch fix) from their ancestry, retaining the pre-fix unconditional --filter=blob:none followed by read-tree and checkout-index without up-front blob refill.

Manual run clearing and requeue were artifacts of unbounded job duration and queue blockage; the mechanism is confirmed through blob-starved oracle tests, GIT_TRACE2_EVENT runtime probes observing 40 sequential fetch RPCs, and successful replication with and without the blob-prefetch fix.

Post-fix verification confirmed no per-blob lazy-fetch mechanism on main; rebased Gerrit 1130 PS5 completed all four matrix cells normally (4m20s–12m15s) instead of hanging, proving the stuck-run pattern is eliminated by both the blob-prefetch fix and pagination repair.
